articles.title: Progressives confront their limited leverage as they take on Democratic leaders
articles.summary: Realistically, the battle to replace the party’s Hill chiefs was built for a disappointing election, not a landslide.
articles.body:
By Corbin Trent's estimate, he's spending 15 hours a day on a cause that has animated the left ever since Democrats won huge majorities in the House and Senate: urging them to dump their leaders.

Trent, a former spokesman for Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, has some well-known allies in his long-shot campaign to oust Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. They include actor Mark Ruffalo, former Ocasio-Cortez chief of staff Saikat Chakrabarti, and countless progressive influencers.

But they don't include Ocasio-Cortez, who underscored on Tuesday that she's backing Jeffries. Even Trent acknowledged that what legions of online progressives are asking for — the rejection of leaders who just presided over Democratic landslides — is unlikely to happen.

"I reckon it's about a 10% chance on Schumer and a 3% chance on Jeffries," Trent told Semafor. "What matters, and matters a lot, is making it loud and clear that voters asked for something else. That it is being denied to them. If you've ever got a chance to beat these folks, you need votes."

Theoretically, the votes to shake up leadership are at least within reach. Informal whip counts and hallway interviews confirm that dozens of newly elected Democrats are interested in challengers to the two New Yorkers who occasionally break from the left. But realistically, the battle to replace Jeffries and Schumer was built for a disappointing election , not a landslide.

And the obstacles of the anti-leadership campaign are revealing the limited reach of a progressive movement that wants to pick the next presidential nominee. Critics of Schumer haven't given up on enlisting Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen to challenge him, but no Democrat has stepped up to take on Jeffries.

Even if Van Hollen mounts a campaign, it will be a massive uphill climb for progressives to deny Schumer the votes in next month's closed-door vote. The left's chances of defeating Jeffries are even lower.

But by forcing the question, progressives hope to either pull off a miracle — or at least, keep an argument going. Activists believe that they, not Schumer and Jeffries, put in the work to win the biggest Democratic victories in decades. The progressive media outlets that exploded after the party's 2024 loss to Trump are now watching the leaders take credit for what they think their movement built.

Their message is consistent: That voters who want "change" and support progressive ideas will stay engaged only if the leadership changes and President Donald Trump is forced to veto big progressive bills.

At last week's post-election Crooked Con, a gathering of progressive activists, strategists, influencers, and podcast addicts, the demand for new leaders hung in the air. Attendees walking up to the Washington Convention Center on Saturday were offered leaflets about stopping bipartisan permitting reform moving through the Senate, warning that it would speed up the building of "immigrant detention centers." (The bill advanced two days later.)

Inside, there were excited murmurs whenever a Democrat was asked about replacing Schumer or Jeffries.

Pressed by Pod Save America co-host Jon Lovett on whether she would challenge Schumer, Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin gave a winding answer that didn't rule it out — but suggested that Schumer could win her over.

"Look, if he wants to be majority leader, what is your plan for the first 100 days?" she said. "How are you going to do things differently so that Democrats get their sh*t together?"

That got muted applause from an audience ready to join an insurgency. There was much more excitement when Rep.-elect Milat Kiros of Colorado said there had been a "mandate" for change, not for current leadership; Kiros unseated Rep. Diana DeGette in one of the left's biggest primary wins.

Everywhere he went, Van Hollen was asked if he would challenge Schumer. In a short interview with Semafor, he disputed the idea that the leader had earned the job already by electing between seven and nine new Democratic senators.

"I'm glad that the DSCC and Senate Majority PAC raised a lot of money," Van Hollen told Semafor. "I mean, their Republican counterparts raised even more money. I think the lesson from this election was, this was people power over money."

The scale of the Democratic wins has made the entire push trickier.

"Look, we had a wonderful, wonderful outcome," said Maurice Mitchell, the president of the Working Families Party, which clashed with DC Democrats over primaries in the Midwest and California. "It's almost like it would be greedy of me to want better outcomes. But I know there were elections that could have been won if we were able to move as a united front."

The modern left is at its most powerful inside the Democratic Party after the party screws things up.

Hillary Clinton's defeat convinced many Democrats, even his Senate colleagues, that Sanders would have won the presidency, and his populist ideas were more popular than whatever it was she ran on. Kamala Harris' defeat was even more empowering for Sanders, whose "Fight Oligarchy" rallies brought out hundreds of thousands of people.

After victory, the left's challenge is twofold. One: Schumer and Jeffries didn't blow it. They are no longer the brittle wimps who were protesting outside of federal buildings last year and insisting they'd "fight" Trump. They beat him.

Two: Democrats really did listen to them. Last year's government shutdown fight, while it did not end as progressives wanted it to, was about healthcare funding — the sort of life-or-death economic issue the left wanted to focus on. The eventual Democratic themes of the election were "costs, chaos, and corruption" and "fighting for an affordable America."

What's worth watching most closely right now is how upstart progressive media — Hasan Piker, Drop Site, Lever, Majority Report, and other influencers — approach all this. Left-leaning media has a much larger reach than it did eight years ago, when Democrats last assembled for an open presidential primary.

They have willed a "leadership challenge" story into existence when most of DC thinks they're bound to fail. They aren't done.

The challenge of actually replacing leaders who just won is already weighing on progressives, who are already asking themselves whether they're undercutting their own allies.

"People are doing what they should be doing, which is swing for the fences. Go after leadership, if that's what people want to do. But if we don't get that, we can't just let it destroy us emotionally," former New York Rep. Jamaal Bowman told Don Lemon on Monday.

Or as Trent put it: "I think it'll be a great thing to highlight when Democrats fail miserably to meet the moment."

In pre-election reporting on Democratic infighting, Axios previewed how the left could lose its leverage: "Anything short of a landslide victory for House Democrats next Tuesday will open the door" to crisis.

articles.title: Does Texas have a state income tax? Here’s what the law, Hinojosa say
articles.summary: Texas has no state income tax and Hinojosa says she doesn't want one. Here is what it would take to change the law and why it is difficult to enact.
articles.body:
Texas is one of a handful of states without a state income tax, and whether that could change was a flashpoint during this year's governor's race .

On the campaign trail, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott released several ads saying his Democratic challenger supports a state income tax and claimed he banned one from ever existing.

However, Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa released her own ad saying that "Texans work harder than anyone," explaining that the state's Constitution bans one and why she opposes creating one.

This rhetoric has led some to ask what it would take for the state to institute a state income tax and whether Hinojosa could do it once she is in office. Here is what she has said about a state income tax and what the law says.

Is Gina Hinojosa for or against a Texas state income tax?

Abbott cited Hinojosa's no vote on House Joint Resolution 38 in 2019 — which sought to create a constitutional amendment banning a state income tax — as his reason for saying Hinojosa supported a state income tax.

However, in an October interview with CBS Texas , she contested what she was voting on, saying she never voted for a state income tax.

"I voted against a repeal of a constitutional ban on an income tax," she said in the interview.

She added that the Texas Constitution already restricted a state income tax through a 1993 amendment championed by then-Lt. Gov. Bob Bullock, a Democrat, which required voters to approve one if the state wanted to institute one.

In 2019, voters approved HJR 38, which replaced that provision with an outright ban.

Not without amending the Texas Constitution, which would take several steps.

Because of HJR 38, also known as Proposition 4 in 2019, Texas lawmakers would need to propose a constitutional amendment to institute a state income tax and repeal the ban.

From there, both chambers would debate it, with Democrats controlling the House and Republicans holding the Senate at the start of the 90th legislative session in January.

After the procedural process, both chambers would need a two-thirds vote to approve the amendment.

Then it would finally go to the Texas voters for approval or denial. A governor cannot enact an income tax or veto a constitutional amendment.

Mateo Rosiles is the Texas Connect reporter for USA TODAY and its regional papers in Texas. Got a news tip for him? Email him at mrosiles@usatodayco.com.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated incumbent Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott on November 3. Hinojosa, a 52-year-old attorney and state lawmaker, is part of a new generation of Democrats who are seeking to attract independents and voters disillusioned by Trump's unpopular war in the Middle East and skyrocketing prices for gas and everyday goods.

articles.title: Democrats investigating sexual harassment allegation against incoming Ohio congressman
articles.summary: An aide claims incoming congressman Brian Poindexter made sexually harassing comments during his campaign.
articles.body:
House Democrats are investigating an aide's complaint that newly elected congressman Brian Poindexter made sexually harassing comments toward her during his campaign.

The investigation is being led by an independent firm hired by the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC), the group confirmed in a statement to CNN.

Poindexter defeated Rep. Max Miller, a former Trump adviser whose ex-wife accused him of domestic violence, which he has denied. The unwelcome development comes as Democrats are trying to focus on building out their agenda on the heels of a massive victory in November.

"The DCCC has been made aware of the allegations and takes them seriously," said Julie Merz, executive director of the campaign group.

In a statement, a spokesperson for Poindexter's campaign said: "Brian gave what he thought was an innocuous compliment to a volunteer. He heard later that it made her feel uncomfortable and he felt awful."

The spokesperson added, "When Brian learned about this, we immediately began to work to get to the bottom of it with an outside HR firm. Neither Brian nor the campaign ever wants anyone to feel uncomfortable."

The Democrats' campaign arm was alerted about the allegation just before the election by the Blue Dog PAC and the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC, the groups said in a statement to CNN. Both groups pulled their endorsement of Poindexter until DCCC finishes its investigation.

"The individual requested that we did not disclose any details about this publicly because she did not want her identity becoming public and she wanted an opportunity to determine how she wanted to proceed while protecting herself," said the statement from both groups. "We respected her desires, and also felt we needed to immediately pull our endorsements pending the investigation being completed. The investigation is ongoing and we await the results."

Poindexter's removal from the two group's endorsement lists came as members were arriving at the Capitol for new member orientation. Sources familiar with the matter told CNN that Poindexter was not invited to the new member orientations for the Progressive Caucus or the Blue Dog Coalition.

Cheyenne Hunt, whose group Reckoning Action is providing support to the anonymous woman, told CNN she was contacted by the aide two days before Poindexter flipped Ohio's 7th District. Hunt described her as a "very low-level staffer" but did not provide additional details in order to protect her anonymity. Hunt declined to discuss the specifics of her allegation.

Lawmakers are in ongoing discussions about how to improve Capitol Hill's handling of sexual harassment claims, following a spate of complaints about other politicians earlier this year. A group of Democrats are pushing for stricter regulations around conduct as part of a rules package for the full House for next year.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has been made aware of the allegation about Poindexter, according to a person familiar with the discussions. His office referred CNN to the campaign arm, pending the ongoing investigation.

Poindexter ran on an economic populist message and played up his background as a union ironworker, but he also leaned into his role as a father. In one early ad, he appeared with his daughters as they ribbed him.

On the campaign trail, Poindexter's history also became a focal point of Miller's attacks against him including a 2013 fight with another man at a baseball game, where he was arrested, and a 1998 incident in which he was arrested by police when they suspected he was in possession of crack cocaine.

Poindexter was never charged in either incident and told CNN in an interview in October he never used hard drugs in his life. He also said he is routinely drug tested for his job and has never failed a test.

articles.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
articles.summary: Georgia GOP Gov. Brian Kemp is also said to be getting encouragement to run.
articles.body:
Supporters and donors have been encouraging Republican Arkansas governor and former White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, according to multiple sources with direct knowledge of the situation.

​When asked about the outreach Sanders has been receiving, her communications director Sam Dubke told ABC News that "Governor Sanders looks forward to serving the people of Arkansas for the next four years."

​Sanders, the daughter of Mike Huckabee, himself a former Arkansas governor, Repubican presidential candidate and current U.S. ambassador to Israel, won re-election as governor last week. She became the first woman ever elected Arkansas governor in 2022.

Before becoming governor, Sanders served as President Donald Trump's press secretary in his first term from July 2017 to June 2019 after having served as deputy press secretary. She was also a senior adviser to Trump's 2016 presidential campaign.

​While Sanders formally briefed the White House press corps less than her predecessors, she became one of Trump's closest and most trusted advisers and has maintained a close relationship with him, having worked for Trump in the White House for 3 1/2 years .

Sanders has long been viewed as a rising star in the Republican Party.

In 2023, a few months after winning the gubernatorial race in Arkansas, Sanders delivered the Republican response to former President Joe Biden's State of the Union address -- remarks usually reserved for individuals seen as on their way up in the party.

Georgia's retiring popular two-term Republican Gov. Brian Kemp is also considering a presidential bid after he leaves office in January and has been encouraged by donors and other Republican officials to run, a source familiar with his thinking told ABC News.

​In the days leading up to the midterm elections, Kemp traveled to South Carolina, one of the early nominating states for Republicans, to campaign for Gov.-elect Alan Wilson.

ABC News has reached out to Kemp's political operation for comment.

​After Republicans' midterm losses, the party is reflecting on what went wrong and how to move forward, with some of those conversations happening publicly.

​Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, who has not ruled out a 2028 presidential run, called Republicans' performance in the midterm elections a " Watergate-level repudiation" of the party.

​Outgoing Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis described the election results as a "meteor strike," arguing that even a "wave" fails to capture the scale of the Republican losses.

​DeSantis is keeping his options open for another presidential run, two people familiar with his thinking told ABC News, after the governor said Florida fended off a blue wave in this year's midterm elections.

articles.title: Lula e Trump: encontro é 'provável' no G20 em Miami, diz ministro | G1
articles.standfirst: Havia expectativa de um encontro entre os presidentes durante cúpula da Asean nas Filipinas, mas, segundo Márcio Elias Rosa, incompatibilidade de agendas não permitiu. Lula e Trump ainda não se reuniram após a reeleição do petista.
articles.summary: Ministro Márcio Elias Rosa afirma que encontro entre Lula e Trump deve ocorrer no G20 em Miami.
articles.body:
O ministro Márcio Elias Rosa (Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio) concede entrevista a jornalistas em Manila, nas Filipinas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O ministro do Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio, Márcio Elias Rosa , afirmou neste sábado (14) que considera "muito provável" um encontro entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) e o presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , durante a cúpula do G20 , que será realizada em Miami nos dias 14 e 15 de dezembro .

Havia a expectativa de que os dois líderes pudessem conversar presencialmente durante a cúpula da Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático (Asean) , nas Filipinas.

No entanto, de acordo com o ministro, o encontro não ocorreu por conta da incompatibilidade entre os compromissos oficiais dos chefes de Estado. Lula sairá das Filipinas neste domingo (15); e Trump deve desembarcar no país na segunda-feira (16).

"Eu acho que é possível que exista um encontro durante o G20 lá em Miami, em dezembro. É muito provável, porque os dois presidentes estarão no mesmo ambiente e não há nada que impeça que eles se encontrem. Só não vão se encontrar aqui [nas Filipinas], porque a agenda, de fato, não permitiu", declarou Márcio Elias Rosa, que acompanha Lula na viagem internacional.

🔎O G20 é um fórum de cooperação econômica que reúne as maiores economias do mundo para discutir questões financeiras globais.

Lula e Donald Trump ainda não se reuniram após a reeleição do petista em outubro deste ano. Apesar de dizer que gosta de Lula, Trump não cumprimentou o brasileiro pela vitória nas urnas.

Nos dias seguintes à votação no Brasil, o norte-americano evitou dar respostas quando questionado sobre se reconhecia o resultado eleitoral.

Em declarações à imprensa, o presidente americano afirmou que o pleito brasileiro "pareceu ter sido fraudado" , embora tenha sinalizado que pretende conversar com Lula.

O governo dos EUA autorizou a entrada e a permanência, no território americano, de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato que fugiu do Brasil após ser derrotado na disputa presidencial .

Segundo Márcio Elias Rosa, a comitiva brasileira encerra a passagem pela Ásia neste domingo, seguindo para a Espanha antes do retorno definitivo ao Brasil.

Apesar de o encontro com Trump nas Filipinas não ter se concretizado, Márcio Elias Rosa disse que o governo brasileiro tem mantido diálogos com autoridades dos EUA sobre o tarifaço imposto por Trump contra produtos brasileiros.

"As relações com os Estados Unidos estão boas. Nós estamos na expectativa de receber uma proposta de acordo, que eles ficaram de nos encaminhar, cujo prazo deve estar se exaurindo nesta semana", disse o ministro.

O tarifaço imposto pelo governo de Donald Trump contra o Brasil consistiu na aplicação de sobretaxas sobre milhares de produtos exportados por empresas brasileiras.

Fundamentada na Seção 301 da Lei de Comércio americana após uma investigação de quase um ano, a medida foi justificada por Washington sob alegações de práticas comerciais desleais — incluindo impasses alfandegários relacionados ao etanol e críticas ao PIX, por supostamente prejudicar concorrentes de meios de pagamento dos EUA.

Por outro lado, o pacote poupou dezenas de itens estratégicos e de alto volume de exportação, como café, carne bovina, petróleo bruto, aeronaves civis e suco de laranja, para evitar o desabastecimento e o encarecimento de insumos essenciais nos Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Idosos puxam alta do comparecimento no 2º turno e ajudam voto facultativo a atingir maior participação desde 2014 | G1
articles.standfirst: Percentual é 9,4 pontos maior que 2022; entre quem é obrigado a votar, participação fica estável em 83%
articles.summary: Percentual é 9,4 pontos maior que 2022; entre quem é obrigado a votar, participação fica estável em 83%
articles.body:
Idoso de 82 anos vota para 'conviver com a própria consciência' — Foto: Gyovanna Soares/g1

O comparecimento às urnas aumentou do 1º para o 2º turno das eleições de 2026, impulsionado principalmente pelos eleitores que não são obrigados a votar. Segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), 62,7% do eleitorado facultativo participou da votação, a maior taxa entre as quatro últimas eleições gerais. Em 2022, o índice foi de 53,3%.

O movimento ocorreu em meio à queda da abstenção no 2º turno, que ficou em 19,2%, o menor patamar desde 2006 . A mobilização dos idosos, para quem o voto é facultativo a partir dos 70 anos, é apontada como um dos fatores que contribuíram para a vitória histórica do presidente Lula (PT). Após terminar o 1º turno atrás de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), o petista conseguiu uma virada inédita e se reelegeu com mais de 4 milhões de votos de vantagem. Reduzir a ausência de eleitores nas urnas foi uma das prioridades da campanha do PT na reta final da disputa .

QUEM TEM VOTO FACULTATIVO? São os jovens de 16 e 17 anos, os maiores de 70 anos e os analfabetos. Neste ano, o grupo somava 22,2 milhões de eleitores aptos, 14% do eleitorado. Desses, 13,9 milhões foram às urnas no 2º turno.

Em números absolutos, cerca de 2,96 milhões de eleitores a mais foram às urnas no segundo turno, e quase metade deles (49%) tinha voto facultativo. A comparação considera 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos em 5.757 localidades, incluindo as cidades do exterior.

A alta se concentrou entre os eleitores mais velhos e os de menor escolaridade. Em sentido contrário, a abstenção subiu em nove estados, sete deles na região Norte.

Voto facultativo tem a maior participação desde 2014

Têm voto facultativo os jovens de 16 e 17 anos, os maiores de 70 anos e os analfabetos. Neste ano, o grupo somava 22,2 milhões de eleitores aptos, 14% do eleitorado. Desses, 13,9 milhões foram às urnas no segundo turno.

Comparecimento e abstenção do eleitorado facultativo – 2º turno — Foto: Arte/g1

O avanço também aparece na comparação entre os dois turnos deste ano. No primeiro, 56,2% dos eleitores facultativos compareceram. No segundo, foram 62,7%, alta de 6,5 pontos percentuais.

Entre os eleitores obrigados a votar, a diferença entre os turnos foi bem menor: o comparecimento passou de 82,6% para 83,7%.

Percentual de comparecimento dos eleitorados obrigatório e facultativo no 2º turno — Foto: Arte/g1

Dentro do voto facultativo, foram os idosos que puxaram a alta. A abstenção caiu 7,5 pontos entre os eleitores de 70 anos ou mais e 4,3 pontos entre os analfabetos de 18 a 69 anos. Entre os jovens de 16 e 17 anos, recuou só 0,7 ponto, de 12,7% para 12,0%.

Na série desde 2014, a participação de quem é obrigado a votar praticamente não mudou. No segundo turno, ela oscilou entre 82,9% e 83,7%.

Já entre os facultativos, a taxa ficou abaixo de 50% em 2014 e 2018, subiu para 53,3% em 2022 e deu o maior salto agora.

Com isso, a distância entre os dois grupos encolheu. Em 2018, era de 34,3 pontos percentuais. Em 2026, caiu para 21 pontos.

Percentual de comparecimento do eleitorado obrigatório e do facultativo no 2º turno — Foto: Arte/g1

A queda da abstenção cresceu com a idade. Entre os eleitores de 70 a 79 anos, ela passou de 37,9% para 30,5%. Entre os de 80 anos ou mais, de 73,1% para 65,4%. Nas faixas de 16 a 20 anos, a variação foi inferior a 1 ponto.

articles.title: Carne suína brasileira: Ministro negocia fim de veto nas Filipinas | G1
articles.standfirst: André de Paula (Agricultura) disse que tem feito reuniões com autoridades filipinas e que suspensão da importação não deve continuar em 2027, um receio dos produtores brasileiros.
articles.summary: Carne suína brasileira: André de Paula negocia nas Filipinas para assegurar que a suspensão das vendas seja de apenas 60 dias e não prejudique o setor em 2027.
articles.body:
O ministro da Agricultura e Pecuária, André de Paula, afirmou neste sábado (14) que está "otimista" com as negociações do governo brasileiro com autoridades das Filipinas em relação à importação pelo país asiático da carne suína brasileira.

🔎Nesta semana, o governo das Filipinas suspendeu as importações de carne suína . O mercado filipino é o maior comprador da carne suína do Brasil, com 25% do total exportado pelo país. Quase metade da carne suína consumida nas Filipinas é de origem brasileira ( leia mais aqui ).

Em entrevista a jornalistas em Manila, capital das Filipinas, André de Paula afirmou que terá uma reunião com o secretário de Agricultura do país asiático na próxima segunda-feira (16) para tratar do tema.

O ministro destacou que a suspensão da compra da carne suína do Brasil é "uma medida de 60 dias" e, portanto, não deve se estender ao longo de 2027. Esse é um dos receios do governo e de produtores brasileiros.

"Iniciamos uma conversa com os presidentes e ministros. Eu estou muito otimista que nós possamos avançar. Acho que esse balanço será possível na segunda-feira, quando estarei aqui, com a equipe técnica do Ministério, vamos nos reunir com o secretário de Agricultura [das Filipinas] e com a sua equipe técnica", declarou André de Paula.

"Isso vai nos dar oportunidade de conhecer com mais detalhes, mas o que poderia dizer neste momento é que os sinais são positivos, são tranquilizadores e estou muito otimista. Posso afirmar, isso foi colocado pelo próprio presidente, essa é uma medida de 60 dias", completou.

O ministro da Agricultura disse ainda que o governo brasileiro está disposto a aceitar pleitos do governo filipino na área e disse que os dois países têm uma relação "muito boa", "sólida" e de 80 anos.

O governo filipino disse que a decisão de restringir as importações foi tomada para proteger os produtores locais, que aumentaram a produção e pressionam para recuperar o mercado perdido para países com preço mais competitivo, como o Brasil.

A medida afeta todos os países que vendem nove categorias de produtos suínos para as Filipinas – como carnes frescas, congeladas e miúdos

De janeiro a outubro de 2026, o Brasil vendeu mais de 300 mil toneladas em produtos do gênero para o país, negócio de mais de US$ 587 milhões.

articles.title: Escala 5x2: Fux suspende julgamento no STF e leva para o físico | G1
articles.standfirst: Julgamento no plenário virtual tinha 4 votos para manter início da nova escala em 16 de dezembro; agora, tema volta à estaca zero no Supremo
articles.summary: Escala 5x2: Luiz Fux suspende julgamento no STF e leva o caso ao plenário físico, zerando o placar de votos que previa o início da nova jornada em 16 de dezembro.
articles.body:
Ministro Luiz Fux durante julgamento no Supremo — Foto: Luiz Silveira/STF

O ministro Luiz Fux fez um destaque no julgamento sobre a transição da escala 6x1 para a 5x2 e levou o processo para o plenário físico do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). Ainda não há data para a retomada do caso, já que o presidente da Corte, ministro Edson Fachin, precisará colocar a ação em pauta.

No plenário virtual, três ministros já tinham votado e acompanhado o relator Flávio Dino para confirmar as regras definidas pelo ministro para o início da escala 5x2 em 16 de dezembro. Agora, o placar fica zerado e os ministros terão que recomeçar o julgamento.

Enquanto o plenário do STF não toma uma decisão, a liminar de Flávio Dino continua valendo. Nela, o ministro mantém para 16 de dezembro o início da escala 5x2 e permite que, durante a primeira etapa da transição, a jornada de 42 horas semanais seja distribuída em cinco dias.

Esses cinco dias com expedientes de até 8 horas e 24 minutos por dia, sem pagamento de adicional de hora extra pelos 24 minutos que ultrapassam as oito horas.

A regra vale mesmo se não houver acordo ou convenção coletiva até 15 de dezembro ( entenda mais abaixo ).

Os ministros Alexandre de Moraes, Cármen Lúcia e Gilmar Mendes já tinham confirmado as regras definidas por Dino. O plenário virtual iria até 23h59 de 23 de novembro. Agora, cada um dos ministros precisará votar novamente quando Fachin colocar o tema em pauta no plenário do Supremo.

A primeira etapa começa em 16 de dezembro de 2026, quando o limite passa de 44 para 42 horas semanais , com dois dias de repouso remunerado. A redução definitiva para 40 horas semanais está prevista para dezembro de 2027.

Um dos impasses levados ao STF envolvia justamente essa etapa de transição. Como a nova regra manteve o limite ordinário de oito horas diárias, a divisão das 42 horas pelos cinco dias de trabalho resulta em jornadas de oito horas e 24 minutos.

Na liminar agora submetida aos demais ministros, Flávio Dino autorizou esses 24 minutos adicionais sem incidência de hora extra durante o período intermediário, mesmo quando patrões e sindicatos não tiverem chegado a acordo coletivo até 15 de dezembro.

A decisão também afastou travas rígidas de tempo, semanais e mensais, para o aproveitamento dos repousos remunerados.

Com isso, acordos e convenções coletivas poderão definir quando os dois dias de folga serão usufruídos, desde que o direito aos dois descansos seja preservado.

Flávio Dino também estabeleceu prazo de 90 dias para revisão de acordos coletivos , determinou que a redução da jornada não poderá provocar redução salarial e deu 180 dias para o Congresso regulamentar regimes diferenciados para setores específicos e regras de adaptação para micro e pequenas empresas.

articles.title: ‘Tocou o coração’, diz mãe que abençoou moto do filho em cena viral | G1
articles.standfirst: Maria Aparecida, 64 anos, vive momentos de celebridade ao ser reconhecida em Presidente Prudente (SP) e diz que fez o gesto porque se sentiu emocionada. Imagens viralizaram após o filho Thiago Marques, 27, publicar o registro em rede social.
articles.summary: Um vídeo gravado em Presidente Prudente (SP) viralizou nas redes sociais. Ele mostra uma mãe abençoando a moto nova do filho.
articles.body:
Protagonista de uma cena que viralizou na web ao abençoar com água benta a moto zero quilômetro do filho , em Presidente Prudente (SP), Maria Aparecida de Oliveira Marques, de 64 anos, vive dias de celebridade ao ser reconhecida nas ruas. Ao g1 , ela contou que teve o gesto por emoção. "Tocou meu coração", afirma, sobre a conquista do filho e o que a motivou a pedir proteção divina.

Flagrada por câmeras de monitoramento, a mãe de Thiago Aparecido de Oliveira Marques, de 27 anos, aparece segurando uma garrafinha com água benta. Em seguida, ela se aproxima da moto e começa a jogar o líquido sobre o veículo enquanto faz uma prece. Assista acima.

O vídeo, registrado na noite de 23 de outubro, foi compartilhado no perfil de Thiago em uma rede social . Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a postagem já somava quase um milhão de visualizações.

Thiago Marques com a mãe Maria Aparecida e a moto nova abençoada com água benta em Presidente Prudente (SP): momento emocionante com a proteção divina — Foto: Thiago Aparecido de Oliveira Marques/Arquivo pessoal

Com a repercussão da cena, Maria Aparecida afirma que passou a ser reconhecida na rua e agradece pelo carinho recebido. “A minha amiga ligou dizendo: ‘Cida, tá famosa, hein’. Eu não esperava uma coisa dessas, estou muito feliz. Muito obrigada a todos”, contou, ao g1 .

Dizem que bênção de mãe tem poder e, fazendo jus ao ditado, Maria Aparecida transformou a felicidade do filho em um momento com ainda mais significado.

“O Thiago chegou, deixou a moto e foi embora. Tocou meu coração, peguei a garrafinha de água benta e fui lá. Abençoei a moto dele. Fiquei muito feliz”, declara ela, ao g1 .

Ao g1 , o jovem, que é empresário no ramo de peças de moto, descreveu a emoção que sentiu após ver o gesto espontâneo da mãe.

“Na hora que percebi minha mãe jogando água benta na minha moto nova, minha primeira reação foi de surpresa e emoção. Eu tinha acabado de pegar a moto zero quilômetro naquele dia e, à noite, me deparei com aquela cena tão inesperada e cheia de significado.”

Maria Aparecida joga água benta e abençoa moto zero do filho Thiago Marques em Presidente Prudente (SP): cena viralizou na web — Foto: Thiago Aparecido de Oliveira Marques/Arquivo pessoal

Para o filho, atitude de Maria Aparecida reforçou a conexão que existe entre os dois. Ele disse que o sentimento foi uma mistura de felicidade, gratidão e amor.

“Naquele momento, percebi que não era apenas uma bênção para a moto, mas uma demonstração do amor e da preocupação dela comigo. A moto é uma conquista material, mas ter uma mãe que ora por você e pede a proteção de Deus em cada passo da sua vida não tem preço. Foi uma cena simples, mas que tocou profundamente meu coração", ressaltou.

Devota de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, padroeira do Brasil, a mãe de Thiago sempre pede para que o filho tenha cuidado no trânsito. O rapaz pilota moto desde 18 anos e já teve cinco veículos, mas seu grande sonho era uma motocicleta zero.

“Quando eu tinha 18 anos e tinha acabado de tirar minha habilitação, sofri um acidente de moto. Uma mulher acabou me atropelando porque não respeitou a placa de ‘pare’. Foi uma situação que marcou bastante, principalmente para a minha mãe”, relembra.

O acidente continua sendo marcante para Maria Aparecida e pode ter influenciado na atitude de abençoar a nova conquista do filho.

“Acredito que isso também explica o gesto dela de abençoar minha moto nova. Por trás daquela atitude existe uma mãe que já passou por um susto, que sabe dos riscos e que, independentemente da idade que o filho tenha, nunca deixa de se preocupar. No fundo, o que ela mais quer é me ver realizando meus sonhos, mas sempre protegido e com saúde", concluiu o jovem.

Para Thiago, de Presidente Prudente (SP), atitude da mãe Maria Aparecida de jogar água benta na moto reforça a conexão entre os dois — Foto: Thiago Aparecido de Oliveira Marques/Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Lula cancela discurso e declaração à imprensa nas Filipinas por causa de rouquidão | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente está com voz falha há mais de 15 dias. Especialistas apontam efeitos da radioterapia de 2011, cicatrizes da cirurgia de 2022, desgaste da campanha e idade entre as hipóteses; só o exame da laringe, porém, esclarece a causa.
articles.summary: Presidente está com voz falha há mais de 15 dias. Especialistas apontam efeitos da radioterapia de 2011, cicatrizes da cirurgia de 2022, desgaste da campanha e idade entre as hipóteses; só o exame da laringe, porém, esclarece a causa.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) cancelou dois compromissos oficiais neste sábado (14) em Manila, nas Filipinas, por causa da rouquidão que enfrenta há mais de 15 dias. A informação foi confirmada pelo Palácio do Planalto.

O presidente realiza uma visita de Estado ao país . Trata-se da primeira visita oficial de Chefe de Estado brasileiro às Filipinas. Neste domingo (15), o petista participa da Cúpula da Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático (ASEAN).

Os compromissos cancelados neste sábado (14) foram a declaração à imprensa após o encontro com o presidente filipino, Ferdinand Marcos Jr., e o discurso de encerramento do Fórum Empresarial Brasil-Filipinas, organizado pela ApexBrasil.

Lula embarcou para Filipinas na quinta-feira (12). Antes, o presidente estava desde segunda-feira (9) em Antália, na Turquia, onde participou da 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31).

🔎O que pode explicar a voz falha do presidente?

Aos 81 anos, Lula carrega um histórico que costuma alimentar especulações sempre que a voz falha: um câncer de laringe tratado há 15 anos e uma cirurgia nas pregas vocais em 2022.

Radioterapia deixa o tecido menos flexível

O tumor foi descoberto em outubro de 2011. Em vez de operá-lo, os médicos trataram Lula com quimioterapia e radioterapia, que se estenderam até 2012.

Esse tipo de tratamento, explica o otorrinolaringologista Antônio Carlos Cedin, da BP – A Beneficência Portuguesa de São Paulo, provoca inflamação em toda a laringe enquanto dura. O inchaço passa com o tempo, mas a região irradiada pode cicatrizar e ficar endurecida.

O efeito aparece na voz porque o som nasce da vibração das pregas vocais, conhecidas popularmente como cordas vocais, que precisam ser macias e elásticas para vibrar bem.

“Quando a pele se machuca e cicatriza, o tecido que se forma é mais duro e menos elástico que o original. É o que acontece na prega vocal depois da radioterapia, e por isso ela deixa de vibrar como antes”, explica Cedin.

Como num violão, em que a espessura e a tensão da corda mudam o som, uma prega enrijecida vibra menos vezes por segundo, e a voz sai mais grave. A fonoaudióloga Bruna Martinovic acredita que isso tenha acontecido com o presidente, cuja voz mudou desde 2011.

Essa mudança se somou a uma característica antiga. A rouquidão acompanha Lula desde que ele se tornou figura pública, lembra a fonoaudióloga Nara Castanhas Zimermano, conselheira do Conselho Regional de Fonoaudiologia da 2ª Região (Estado de São Paulo).

Segundo ela, a radioterapia também deixa a região ressecada e enfraquece os músculos, o que acrescentou perda de força e de mobilidade a uma voz que já era rouca. Mais de dez anos depois do tratamento, a laringe ainda passaria por uma nova intervenção.

Em novembro de 2022, Lula passou por uma cirurgia na laringe para retirar uma leucoplasia da prega vocal esquerda, uma espécie de ferida esbranquiçada que se forma na mucosa. O exame da lesão não identificou câncer.

A retirada é a conduta usual, segundo Cedin, porque lesões desse tipo podem se transformar em tumor ao longo dos anos se o agente irritante continuar agindo.

Uma das causas possíveis, aponta o médico, é o refluxo, quando o ácido do estômago sobe até a laringe e agride as pregas.

A cirurgia, por sua vez, deixou uma ferida que precisou cicatrizar e acrescentou mais uma cicatriz à região já tratada com radioterapia.

Quem vive de falar em público submete as pregas a uma demanda que o restante da população não tem. Políticos, assim como professores, atores, cantores e jornalistas, são considerados profissionais da voz, e uma campanha eleitoral multiplica a carga: são comícios e caminhadas em que é preciso competir com outros sons, falando alto, muitas vezes com pouco sono.

Martinovic aposta, sem ter examinado o presidente, que o excesso de uso da voz é a hipótese mais forte para o quadro atual. Ela observa que, em alguns momentos, Lula chega a ficar sem voz, e não apenas rouco.

Cedin acrescenta que o uso intenso e tenso da voz causa pequenos traumas nas pregas, de inchaços a hemorragias localizadas, que podem se consolidar em calos só resolvidos com cirurgia. É um risco conhecido entre professores e cantores, e o presidente, observa o médico, fala muito.

A idade entra na conta porque, com o envelhecimento, o organismo perde colágeno e outras proteínas, e os músculos ficam menos fortes e flexíveis. Isso alcança a laringe e também a força do ar expirado, que sustenta a voz.

“O histórico de câncer, a rouquidão que já existia, a idade avançada e uma rotina intensa de uso da voz, na agenda de presidente e na campanha, explicam o desgaste que ele vive agora”, resume Nara.

Diante da rouquidão de alguém que já teve câncer na laringe, a pergunta mais imediata é se o tumor voltou. Os especialistas consideram precipitado seguir por esse caminho. Passados 15 anos do tratamento, e depois de anos de acompanhamento médico, uma pessoa nessa situação é considerada curada.

“Um sintoma isolado como a rouquidão não dá base para dizer que um câncer tratado há tanto tempo voltou”, afirma.

Isso não quer dizer que o sintoma deva ser ignorado. Em doenças da laringe, lembra Cedin, o diagnóstico precoce é o que garante a cura. Quando o problema demora a ser tratado, o caminho pode ser uma cirurgia maior, com retirada de parte da laringe e uma recuperação da voz bem mais difícil.

Por isso, a rouquidão que persiste deve ser avaliada por um médico, que é quem consegue dizer qual é a origem do quadro.

Tratamento depende do que o exame mostrar

É o exame do otorrinolaringologista, em que uma microcâmera é introduzida pelo nariz para observar as pregas, que separa o simples desgaste de uma lesão, como pólipo, calo ou hemorragia. A partir dele, define-se o caminho: medicamentos, procedimentos ou sessões com fonoaudiólogo, que combinam exercícios e, em alguns casos, laser de baixa potência.

Em qualquer cenário, o repouso da voz é a base, porque é ele que tira a pessoa do pico de afonia, explica Nara. Em quadros de desgaste como o descrito por ela, a voz costuma sair áspera, com muito escape de ar, tensa e com perda de potência.

Para reverter o cenário, entram também exercícios de aquecimento, fortalecimento e desaquecimento vocal, além de hidratação e do afastamento de irritantes, como fumaça, poluição e o ar seco do ar-condicionado.

Martinovic recomenda de 2 a 3 litros de água por dia e inalação com soro, que leva umidade direto às vias respiratórias.

Lula contou que tem tomado chá para recuperar a voz. O chá quente ajuda como complemento, pelo calor e pela hidratação, mas não age sobre a causa da rouquidão, segundo Cedin, já que a bebida segue pelo esôfago, atrás da laringe, e não chega às pregas, por onde só passa ar.

As marcas da radioterapia persistem como sequela, e os cuidados com a voz, segundo os especialistas, devem durar a vida toda, com acompanhamento regular de um fonoaudiólogo. Isso não impede uma voz funcional: mesmo alterada desde 2011, a de Lula atravessou campanhas e quatro anos de governo sem comprometer o entendimento do que ele diz.

Com repouso e terapia vocal, avalia Nara, há margem para melhora e para que o presidente volte a discursar com mais tranquilidade. Quanto ao episódio atual, a explicação e o tratamento dependem de um exame que só o próprio presidente pode fazer.

articles.title: Lula nas Filipinas: parceria em semicondutores e minerais críticos | G1
articles.standfirst: País asiático tem desenvolvido indústria de chips enquanto Brasil possui a segunda maior reserva de terras raras do mundo. Lula fez postagem nas redes sociais sobre visita a Manila.
articles.summary: Lula e o presidente Ferdinand Marcos Jr. discutem a integração entre as reservas de minerais críticos do Brasil e a indústria de semicondutores das Filipinas.
articles.body:
Lula se encontra com o presidente das Filipinas, Ferdinand Marcos Jr, em Manila — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/Presidência da República

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) afirmou neste sábado (14) que o Brasil e as Filipinas têm potencial para integrar cadeias produtivas nas áreas de minerais críticos, semicondutores e microeletrônica.

A declaração foi feita em uma publicação nas redes sociais durante visita oficial a Manila , capital do país asiático, onde o petista se encontrou com o presidente filipino Ferdinand Marcos Jr .

Segundo Lula , a ideia é aproximar centros de pesquisa, universidades e empresas dos países na área. O Brasil detém a segunda maior reserva global de terras raras . Já as Filipinas possuem um parque industrial voltado à montagem e produção de chips e componentes eletrônicos .

"Na área de ciência e tecnologia, vamos aproximar centros de pesquisa, universidades e empresas inovadoras dos dois países. Como polos regionais de inovação, Brasil e Filipinas têm muito a ganhar com a integração de cadeias de minerais críticos, semicondutores e microeletrônica", disse o presidente após o encontro com Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

🔋Os minerais críticos, como lítio, níquel, cobalto, cobre e elementos de terras raras, são matérias-primas essenciais para fabricar baterias, equipamentos de energia limpa e componentes eletrônicos avançados. Os semicondutores, utilizados em celulares, computadores, carros e equipamentos militares, dependem diretamente desses insumos processados.

Entre os ministros que acompanham Lula na viagem a Manila, estão Alexandre Silveira (Minas e Energia), Márcio Elias Rosa (Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio), Mauro Vieira (Relações Exteriores) e André de Paula (Agricultura e Pecuária).

No X, Lula destacou que esta é a primeira visita de um presidente brasileiro ao país asiático, com o qual o Brasil celebra 80 anos de relações diplomáticas.

Nas Filipinas, o petista participa da Cúpula da Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático (ASEAN). Também está prevista a participação do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , no evento.

O mercado filipino é o maior comprador da carne de porco do Brasil, com 25% do total exportado pelo país. Quase metade da carne suína consumida nas Filipinas é de origem brasileira.

Na viagem ao país asiático, a comitiva brasileira deve tratar do tema. A principal preocupação é evitar que a restrição de importações se estenda por 2027 .

Lula foi recebido com uma apresentaçã na chegada à Base Aérea Villamor, em Manila, capital das Filipinas — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/Presidência da República

articles.title: Teresópolis certifica profissionais em curso sobre autismo e inclusão | G1
articles.standfirst: Capacitação reúniu participantes de diversas áreas e Câmara Municipal recebeu reconhecimento por ações voltadas à acessibilidade e ao acolhimento de pessoas com deficiência.
articles.summary: Capacitação reúniu participantes de diversas áreas e Câmara Municipal recebeu reconhecimento por ações voltadas à acessibilidade e ao acolhimento de pessoas com deficiência.
articles.body:
Câmara de Teresópolis certifica — Foto: Divulgação

A Câmara Municipal de Teresópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, realizou, nesta quarta-feira (11), uma sessão especial para a entrega dos certificados do Curso de Capacitação Básica em Autismo e Pessoas com Deficiência (PcD).

A iniciativa, promovida pela Incluir Treinamentos e Certificação, reuniu profissionais de diferentes áreas interessados em ampliar a qualificação para o atendimento de pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) e deficiência.

Segundo a organização, Teresópolis passou a concentrar o maior número de profissionais certificados como Amigos do Autista e das Pessoas com Deficiência no estado do Rio de Janeiro. A formação teve como objetivo estimular práticas mais inclusivas, acessíveis e humanizadas nos serviços prestados à população.

Durante a cerimônia, a Câmara Municipal recebeu o reconhecimento de primeira Casa Legislativa do estado certificada como instituição parceira da inclusão, em razão das ações desenvolvidas em prol da acessibilidade e do acolhimento.

A realização do curso contou com o apoio da vereadora Érika Marra, defensora de políticas públicas voltadas à inclusão. O presidente da Câmara, Luciano Santos, também participou da formação e recebeu o certificado ao lado dos demais participantes.

A formação foi ministrada por Paola Vitalina, representante da Incluir Treinamentos e Certificação, homenageada com um Voto de Congratulações pelo trabalho na qualificação de profissionais e na promoção de iniciativas inclusivas.

De acordo com os organizadores, a ação contribui para o fortalecimento da rede de apoio às pessoas com TEA e deficiência no município, reforçando o compromisso de Teresópolis com a construção de uma sociedade mais acessível e inclusiva.

articles.title: Silicon Valley plots Jensen Huang’s comeback
articles.summary: The tech industry is already thinking of ways the ousted Nvidia chief could return to a seat in power.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — A day after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, Silicon Valley is already anticipating his comeback.

As a close ally of Donald Trump, regularly taking calls — even publicly — from the president, Huang became one of the most prominent and influential voices in Washington for the largely California-based tech industry, leaving a vacuum with his departure from one of the world's most profitable companies that has become the backbone of the AI boom.

But while national security hawks and tech skeptics in Washington prepare to haul him before Congress to bring further scrutiny of his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, Silicon Valley leaders are mourning his swift exit and positing ways that he could return.

The founder of defense tech giant Anduril, Palmer Luckey , and Perplexity AI CEO Aravind Srinivas have rushed to Huang's defense, while SpaceXSI CEO Elon Musk has even floated the idea of hiring him.

Five other tech industry insiders also told POLITICO they expect Huang to eventually return in a major way to leadership within Silicon Valley. Another three were not quite as confident, but indicated they wouldn't be surprised if it happened.

"It is inevitable, with all of the value that he's created and his role commonly accepted as the godfather of AI, that he will have a second act," said an executive at a prominent California startup who was granted anonymity to frankly discuss industry dynamics. "And that any number of hyperscalers and startups are tripping over themselves to reach out to him and bring him on, regardless of any transgressions."

Despite losing his lofty perch at Nvidia, Huang still has a net worth of roughly $145 billion , an ecosystem of connections in high places and a sterling entrepreneurial reputation within the industry, some noted.

"That kind of influence doesn't just disappear overnight," said Joseph Hoefer, chief AI officer at the lobbying firm Monument Advocacy. "I wouldn't confuse losing his position with losing his ability to shape what comes down the road."

A spokesperson for Huang did not respond to a request for comment on his future plans.

Three of the people who spoke with POLITICO said it would be easier for Huang to start a new venture using his wealth of capital, rather than joining an already established company.

The connection to allegations of espionage "would make it much harder for any public company to bring him on board in a leadership role," said Scott Gerber, partner at the tech strategy consultancy Vrge.

Others have started to seize on questions about the initial reports of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, potentially undercutting any support for his ouster. Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), who will likely be the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, told POLITICO this week that he's unsure whether Huang's paramour was knowingly providing information to China based on briefings from U.S. intelligence officials.

David Sacks, Trump's former AI czar and a venture capitalist prominent on the tech right, highlighted reports that some in the U.S. intel community have similar doubts. "The spy narrative is collapsing already," he wrote in an X post .

Recouping influence in Washington, however, may still be trickier than in Silicon Valley. Huang has been a commanding voice in advocating for looser restrictions on exports to China of advanced semiconductors — necessary for the development of artificial intelligence. That position is being called into question by lawmakers in Congress, given an initial Financial Times report that U.S. intelligence believed Huang was having an affair with a spy.

"His standing in industry might be recoverable over time," said Philip Reiner, CEO of the Institute for Security and Technology think tank in California and a former senior director at the National Security Council. "Rebuilding credibility in Washington on China policy is extremely challenging."

Even still, much of the cachet he built was specifically connected to Trump's White House, meaning it would have an expiration date regardless, ahead of the 2028 election, others noted.

"[M]uch of his political influence was tied to his relationship with the current administration, and that kind of access will be hard to rebuild once the political landscape shifts," said Nu Wexler, a principal at Four Corners Public Affairs who advises tech companies on policy communications.

This delicate position raises the stakes for an upcoming House hearing on the scandal, for which Huang has agreed to testify .

"If he can come before Congress and own mistakes, but also explain them and still be a credible voice, that will go a long way towards opening the door for anything else that he would want to do in Washington and the private sector," said Daniel Castro, president of the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation — a think tank funded by Big Tech companies like Amazon and Microsoft.

articles.title: Kreiss-Tomkins becomes first Democrat since 1998 elected governor in Alaska
articles.summary: JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — Alaska voters have elected a Democrat for governor for the first time since 1998, part of a national midterm elections wave that gave t...
articles.body:
JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — Alaska voters have elected a Democrat for governor for the first time since 1998, part of a national midterm elections wave that gave the party sweeping wins in state governments across the country.

Former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans, including one endorsed by President Donald Trump. His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.

Kreiss-Tomkins, often referred to as JKT, completed a political comeback three years after leaving the state House. He traveled throughout Alaska to build his coalition and focused on affordability, advocated for full funding of public schools and called for all oil and gas producers to pay corporate income tax. He also sought a moratorium on new data centers until state lawmakers pass regulations for their development.

He said Alaska had become "broken" under eight years of outgoing Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy and needed a change. He cited among other issues a state ferry system that he said has been left in shambles, with routes to many communities cut drastically. The ferry is a key mode of transportation for southeast Alaska communities not connected by roads, some of which also have limited air service.

Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, emphasized a willingness to work across party lines and said he wanted a Cabinet with Republicans, Democrats and independents.

"If they're competent, if they're service-minded, if they're entrepreneurial, if they're problem-solvers, you're on the team. Game on," he said during a candidate forum last month. "Let's go, and let's get Alaska back on track."

Republican U.S. Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who has at times been at odds with her party, including Trump, endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins a week before the election. She said Kreiss-Tomkins "understands that governing requires listening to people with different perspectives and finding common ground to solve the problems all of us face."

Three former governors including Democrat Tony Knowles, independent Bill Walker and Republican Frank Murkowski, the senator's father, also endorsed him.

In a statement declaring victory earlier Friday, Kreiss-Tomkins said voters wanted change and "a government that works across party lines to move Alaska forward. Our administration will not waste a single day getting to work to solve problems for Alaska." He said his campaign had more than 10,000 donors.

His campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment after The Associated Press called the race.

He defeated Republicans Bernadette Wilson, Dave Bronson and Treg Taylor. Trump had endorsed Wilson, a business owner, and criticized the other Republican candidates for staying in the race. Bronson is a former mayor of Anchorage, Alaska's largest city, while Taylor was a state attorney general under Dunleavy.

Bronson congratulated Kreiss-Tomkins on social media and wished him success. A message seeking comment from Wilson's campaign was not immediately returned.

Many Republicans saw ranking as their party's best shot of retaining the governor's seat. It was a message that conflicted with that of Trump, who has consistently complained about Alaska's unusual voting method, including during a rally in Alaska in October.

Kreiss-Tomkins finished first in August's open primary, followed by a second Democrat, Tom Begich, who withdrew from the race. Begich's campaign at the time said it had concluded that the "strongest path to victory is to bring Democratic voters, donors and resources together behind one candidate." Wilson finished third in the primary.

Kreiss-Tomkins said compromise "is a virtue, not a dirty word," and said he saw the mission of the new governor as working with lawmakers to resolve longstanding problems in the state.

The state's last Democratic governor, Tony Knowles, left office in 2002 after serving back-to-back terms. Walker served from 2014 to 2018.

Kreiss-Tomkins will be sworn in Dec. 7. His lieutenant governor is Zac Johnson, an independent.

articles.title: Texas’s Democratic gov.-elect vows to trade GOP culture wars for moderation
articles.summary: AUSTIN - GOP Gov. Greg Abbott and conservative state lawmakers tried to label incoming Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa a closet progressive, warning that s...
articles.body:
Texas’s Democratic gov.-elect vows to trade GOP culture wars for moderation

AUSTIN - GOP Gov. Greg Abbott and conservative state lawmakers tried to label incoming Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa a closet progressive, warning that she'll turn the deeply red state socialist.

But after Hinojosa's historic upset win amid a blue wave that swept every state office, Texas's first Latina governor-elect vowed during an interview with The Washington Post to avoid culture wars in favor of something Texas hasn't seen in a generation: moderation. On a number of key issues facing her state - affordability, border security, data centers and school vouchers - Hinojosa is staking out what she calls populist positions that seem calibrated to appeal to voters at both ends of the political spectrum. That includes her pledge to work with President Donald Trump on immigration.

"I agree with President Trump that our border needs to be secure and people should not be coming here to cross into the country," Hinojosa said at the state Capitol on Friday. "It's a dangerous journey and I don't think it will be fruitful for them."

In a Truth Social post Thursday about migrant caravans forming in Mexico, Trump referred to her as "the very liberal new governor of Texas." Hinojosa, seated near a photo of the state's last Democratic Gov. Ann Richards, said the Trump administration had not contacted her and she had not spoken to the president, "but I welcome that conversation."

"Trump and I won the same border communities: I won them this time, he won them last time" in 2024, said Hinojosa, who will preside over the country's second-largest Latino population. Latino voters in places like her native Rio Grande Valley were instrumental in Democratic wins, including one county that swung away from Republicans by more than any other in the nation.

Asked if she would end Operation Lone Star, the more than $11 billion-dollar state border security operation Abbott used emergency powers to launch in 2021, Hinojosa said she would review its legality.

"It's essential that we have strong partnership with Washington … to make sure our local border communities are safe," she said.

But she drew a distinction between border security and federal immigration enforcement in Texas's interior. "The election was a referendum on how people are treated within our state, not outside of it, certainly not outside the country," she said.

After a migrant was fatally shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in Houston in July, and another ICE agent was indicted on federal assault charges there last month, Hinojosa stressed that federal agents securing the border was "very different from interior enforcement, which as we have all seen has been chaotic and dangerous and people died, people have been hurt. People are scared and angry and people's rights are violated and that has to stop."

Last week, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, a Democrat, said he was directing police officers to limit their cooperation with ICE during traffic stops. That means he is challenging a policy imposed on the state's largest city by Abbott, who had threatened to withhold state grant funding.

Hinojosa said it was "wrong" for Abbott to require city police "to hold people for ICE who were, for instance, reporting domestic violence assault. That is not good for public safety. That makes us less secure when people don't feel that they can report crimes freely or face being handed over to ICE."

Hinojosa said she will not challenge Texas's mostly Democratic municipal leaders if they block police from cooperating with ICE. But she also said she will not overturn a state law requiring sheriffs and counties that operate jails to comply with ICE.

"I will always follow the law. The law is what it is. It's up to the legislature if that's going to get changed," she said.

The Texas governor has virtually unlimited emergency powers, which some GOP state lawmakers have said they fear Hinojosa will use to overturn conservative laws passed in recent years, including laws requiring people to use bathrooms that match their sex at birth, bans on abortion and gender transition medical care for minors.

Hinojosa said those fears are unfounded.

"I don't see us trying to tackle culture wars. That was not the mandate we were given," she said. "The mandate we were given was to deliver for Texans."

On day one, she said, she plans to declare a "high-cost emergency," freeze electricity rates and suspend the 20-cent-per-gallon state gas and diesel tax. She also plans to immediately issue an emergency proclamation to the legislature to approve a measure that would send every Texas household $1,500.

"That is the emergency that families are experiencing in their homes right now: They just can't afford basics. They can't pay their electric bills. They can't afford to put food on the table. They can't afford to see the doctor," she said.

Abbott had embraced Islamophobia, vowing to "ban sharia law," blocking Muslim housing developments and designating the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the country's largest Muslim civil rights and advocacy organization, a terrorist group. Hinojosa said she would remove that designation.

"We have to use public safety measures for public safety," she said, dismissing what she called "nonsense happening with power that should be used for public safety, money that should use for public safety, that is not being used for safety."

She promised once she's inaugurated Jan. 19 to declare a moratorium on data centers, but only those that have yet to receive state permits because "if they've already received state permits, I don't have the power just to shut them down."

But Hinojosa acknowledged that "there are communities who are under the impression that their water will be shut off if there's only enough water for either them or the data centers."

"I would intervene with all my power to stop that from happening," she said, citing recent water shortages in Corpus Christi. "It can just never be the case that industry is prioritized over people for water that they drink and need to live."

Hinojosa, who like Abbott is Catholic, has said she personally opposes capital punishment. Texas has executed more than 600 death row inmates since the reinstatement of capital punishment in 1976, with an execution scheduled later this month.

But unlike outgoing California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D), who this month began the process of commuting the sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row, Hinojosa said she would consider those on Texas's death row "on a case-by-case basis and review and make a decision in accordance with the law."

Hinojosa voted against the state's abortion ban but during her campaign she also released an ad in which she spoke about her decision to carry her first pregnancy to term even after genetic testing revealed a fetal anomaly. Since the abortion ban went into effect, Texas lawmakers increased funding to $200 million for more than 100 antiabortion pregnancy centers under a state program Hinojosa said she would review and potentially veto.

"My understanding is a lot of that funding was not going to actually provide health care services for women. It should be," she said. "I'm going to take a fine-tooth comb to that entire budget … If it is not serving Texans, not serving their health care needs, not serving families, then, yeah, I would veto that funding."

While Hinojosa voted against a state school voucher program and vowed on the campaign trail to fight it, she said that instead of executive action, she plans to work with the legislature to reshape the program, potentially using it to expand access to prekindergarten.

"It's going to all be one big negotiation," she said.

Hinojosa spoke out during her campaign against mid-decade redistricting her GOP colleagues forced through the legislature last summer despite a Democratic quorum break. But she said she doesn't have to power to reverse it.

"That's something that the legislature would have to pass a law to do," she said.

Republicans retained their majority in the state Senate, and some have suggested they may use Senate rules to strip the incoming Democratic lieutenant governor of her power to lead the senate, effectively blocking Democrats' legislation and the governor's priorities.

But Hinojosa said Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin has been "working with her team to ensure that the voice of the voters is heard, and the voters voted for change."

Hinojosa was elected to the state legislature almost a decade ago, and said she has worked with Republicans on education and other issues, including a former GOP colleague she included on her transition team. She noted she'll have help from two Democratic state senators - Nathan Johnson, who was elected attorney general, and Sarah Eckhardt, the comptroller-elect.

Walking the halls of the Capitol on Friday, Hinojosa shook hands with voters and children in tour groups, all of whom congratulated her. She visited the empty floors of the state House and Senate, pointing out the clear line of sight between them.

"I am hearing very positive feedback from senators who are looking forward to working with me," Hinojosa said. "I know how the legislative process works. I know these people. I know what's important to them. And I know how to get things done here."

articles.title: Why US Democrats are expected to keep Schumer and Jeffries in power
articles.summary: The prospect of keeping the Congressional leaders in power is exposing long-running tensions in the party.
articles.body:
Over a week after Democrats rode a historic wave of support to retake the United States Congress, divisions within the party seem to be threatening to undermine its newfound political momentum.

Despite growing calls for a change in Congressional leadership, Democrats Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries appear likely to remain at the helm of their respective US Senate and House caucuses.

After amassing the most Democratic power in Washington since 2009, the two New Yorkers are seeking to retain their leadership positions as their party prepares to take control of both chambers in January.

Schumer, the US Senate’s 75-year-old minority leader, is vying to lead Democrats’ new majority in the chamber, a post he previously held during Joe Biden’s presidency. On the other side of the US Capitol, the 56-year-old Jeffries, as the current minority leader in the US House, is seeking the top role of speaker, placing him second in the line of succession for the US presidency.

But the prospect of keeping Schumer and Jeffries in charge has frustrated some Democrats, exposing long-running tensions between Democratic lawmakers who want to maintain continuity and those who believe their midterm victories offer an opportunity to fundamentally reshape the party’s priorities.

Here’s why Schumer and Jeffries could prevail:

An election victory buys political goodwill

Perhaps the biggest reason the top two Democrats in the US Congress will hold onto their posts: the party’s massive electoral gains.

Schumer’s supporters argue he helped Democrats secure at least eight Republican-held Senate seats, including victories in traditionally conservative states. The party is poised to hold as many as 56 seats in the next Congress, giving it a substantial majority not seen since former President Barack Obama’s first term in office.

“When the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract”, Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego, with Schumer by his side, told reporters on Tuesday. “And this has been a really good election cycle for us”.

Schumer also played a central role in recruiting candidates who could compete in states where Democrats have struggled in recent elections, including former Ohio Senator Sherrod Brown and former North Carolina Governor Roy Cooper .

Adam Jentleson, a longtime US Senate aide and author of, Supermajority: How Democrats Can Build Lasting Power, argued Schumer’s electoral success makes it difficult for critics to mount a successful challenge.

“It’s hard to argue with somebody who just oversaw the biggest election the Democrats have had since Watergate,” Jentleson said during an interview with public radio station WBUR earlier this month.

“The only people who matter are the members of the Democratic caucus,” Jentleson said, explaining that lawmakers who had recently benefitted from the midterm results would have little incentive to remove the person who helped deliver those victories.

Schumer’s allies have made a similar argument. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand of New York, who oversees the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, credited Schumer’s candidate recruitment and fundraising efforts for helping the party reclaim the US Senate.

“That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership,” she said.

Schumer himself has expressed confidence that he has enough support to retain the position.

In an interview with The Washington Sun on Wednesday, he said he had secured more than enough backing from his colleagues.

“I am going to be elected leader, OK, and we’re united on the issues,” Schumer told the Sun. “We’re united.”

Not every Democrat believes last week’s victories are enough to anoint Schumer as the party’s leader in the Senate in the next Congress.

Senator Chris Van Hollen announced on Thursday he would mount a challenge for the role after factions of the Democratic base, particularly progressives, have called for new leadership.

The Maryland Democrat attracted attention at the start of US President Donald Trump’s second term after he travelled to El Salvador to meet with his constituent, Kilmar Abrego Garcia , who had been deported to the country despite a judge’s ruling barring his removal.

That, according to a senior Senate Democratic aide who spoke with Al Jazeera, exemplified “the fight Schumer just doesn’t have”.

“This is not about any one individual, but it is about answering the call of the American people,” Van Hollen said during a Thursday appearance on MSNOW, adding that US voters sent a message to “reject the status quo and to reject business as usual”.

Another Senate aide, who would only speak on condition of anonymity to talk freely about an internal matter, suggested Van Hollen’s bid may be more about extracting concessions from Schumer, like a promise to serve as a short-term “bridge” to a new generation of Democratic leadership.

An analysis by Al Jazeera showed that 12 Democratic senators have publicly committed to backing Schumer in next month’s leadership election. At least 10 senators, including independent Bernie Sanders, who caucuses with the Democrats, have said they will not. However, only half of those opposed to Schumer’s leadership have backed Van Hollen’s challenge.

In an interview with The Nation published on Wednesday, the Vermont independent senator acknowledged knowing Schumer for decades and even liking him personally. But he argued that personal relationships should not determine who leads the party.

“In this moment in American history, Chuck’s views are way out of touch with where the American people are at — and especially with where [the base of] the Democratic Party is,” Sanders said.

He added that Schumer was not in tune with Democratic voters on the issues, arguing the party needed a new and more ambitious direction.

Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin has also questioned Schumer’s leadership, calling for a concrete plan outlining how Democrats intend to use their newly won congressional power.

Slotkin went further on Tuesday, suggesting to reporters at the US Capitol that senators withhold a quorum — the minimum number of lawmakers required to conduct official business — if Schumer runs unopposed, until he presents a plan that gives members a meaningful voice in setting the party’s priorities.

Georgia Senator Raphael Warnock has also declined to commit to supporting Schumer, telling CNN on Tuesday that Democrats are at an “inflection point” and any senator who believes they should lead deserves an opportunity to make their case.

Still, there is a difference between public dissatisfaction and the votes needed to remove a leader. Senate Democrats select their leader through a private ballot, requiring only a simple majority of the caucus.

Tre Easton, vice president for public policy at the Searchlight Institute and a former deputy chief of staff for Democratic Senator John Fetterman, has also questioned the timing of the push against Schumer, arguing calls for new leadership would have carried more weight following the Democrats’ losses in 2024 rather than immediately after their electoral successes in 2026.

“The job of the leader in each legislative chamber here in the U.S. isn’t to articulate a vision for the party”, Easton said in a social media post. “It’s to keep each respective caucus together and count votes. Dassit”.

Jeffries faces a different kind of challenge

The outlook is considerably clearer for Jeffries, who is seeking to become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes on January 3.

Unlike Schumer, Jeffries does not face a prominent challenger for his leadership position, despite criticism from some progressives over his approach to Trump and his longstanding support for Israel.

His backing from moderate Democrats has been particularly visible.

The New Democrat Coalition, a group of Democratic centrists representing 142 current and newly elected lawmakers, issued a statement on Tuesday endorsing his bid for speaker.

“Hakeem Jeffries is the right person at the right time to lead our party”, the group said. “He’s smart, strategic, and action-oriented, with strong relationships across the Democratic caucus”.

The coalition added that it “can’t wait to vote for Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker of the House on January 3, 2027”.

But support from the party’s moderate wing has not eliminated dissatisfaction among progressives.

Representative Pramila Jayapal, a former chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, said she is withholding her support for Jeffries unless he commits to advancing Medicare for All, a proposal to establish a government-funded universal healthcare system.

Jayapal has also acknowledged that the lack of an alternative candidate complicates the leadership debate.

“You can’t beat somebody with nobody,” the Washington state Democrat told Talking Points Memo, adding that the emergence of a challenger would change the calculations of lawmakers considering whether to support Jeffries.

Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York, meanwhile, was asked by CNN whether she supported Jeffries.

“The race is unopposed. Yeah,” she responded, suggesting that the absence of a challenger was an important factor in the debate.

The tensions in the US House have also been illustrated by the case of Don Leonard, an incoming Democratic congressman from Ohio who said he will withhold his support for Jeffries unless the party commits to specific policy changes.

Leonard, who has called for an end to US support for Israel and the war in Iran, alleged in a video posted to social media that senior House Democrats threatened to make his life a “living hell” in Washington and undermine his chances of re-election in 2028 if he continued attaching conditions to his support for Jeffries.

He has not identified the lawmakers involved, and the allegations have not been independently verified. House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar told reporters on Tuesday he did not know which senior Democrats Leonard was referring to.

Jeffries, who has denied reports that US House Democrats have been receiving calls to oppose his bid for the speakership, spoke to reporters on Thursday about frustrations within the party over his leadership.

“We take nothing for granted, because all of us in the House of Representatives are on a two-year employment contract”, Jeffries said. “And we have to continue to make our case both with respect to our track record up until this point, as well as, perhaps even more importantly, our vision for the future”.

The pressure will come after the leadership votes

The leadership contests are scheduled for November 18 and 19 for House Democrats and at an unannounced date in December for Senate Democrats.

If elected, both Schumer and Jeffries will likely continue to face competing demands from progressives seeking more aggressive action against Trump and from moderates representing districts and states where a more centrist approach may be politically important.

They will also have to contend with the practical limitations of governing. Even with control of both chambers, Democrats will not have the 60 Senate votes generally required to overcome a filibuster, meaning they will need Republican support for much of their legislation.

For now, however, the party’s electoral gains have given Schumer and Jeffries an argument for continuity.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” Schumer wrote in an X post on Thursday. “I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together—55 seats and counting is an amazing result—and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader.”
